text: Scope is locked. Now the first real architecture decision: exactly how BrennanERP gets protected against the failure that cost two days of production visibility.

The real constraint is what actually broke: one server, one storage array, no independent secondary copy anywhere. Failover has to be automatic, and the recovery time target has to be proven with a real drill, not assumed.

Log shipping leaves the secondary behind and needs a human to fail it over. Database mirroring is deprecated. A Failover Cluster Instance alone still shares one storage array between both nodes -- it wouldn't have survived the same failure.
The chosen design: SQLDBA01 and SQLDBA02, each with independent storage, joined into BrennanWSFC, running BrennanAG with BrennanERP from day one, reachable through one stable name, BrennanAGListener.
The stack is chosen and the names are locked. Next: planning the Windows Server Failover Cluster itself, before a single node gets built.
